At home and at work, I get stuck on this feeling that things have to be just so. In my office, the pens on my desk need to be evenly spaced, the folders in the cabinet all at the same height. If a student moves a chair slightly off-center, I catch myself fixing it before I even realize I’m doing it. It’s not that I enjoy it; it just feels wrong in my body if things are off, like a tension that doesn’t ease until I “fix” it.  

Lately it’s been more about food and my body. I’m constantly thinking about what I’ve eaten, checking labels, cutting things into exact portions. If I feel like I’ve eaten “too much,” I’ll wash my hands and wipe the counters repeatedly, like I’m trying to erase it somehow. I’m showering longer, and I sanitize the kitchen a lot after meals.  

It’s not completely taking over my life, but it’s starting to crowd my thoughts, especially around meals and in my office.

I’ll spend 20 minutes adjusting the diplomas on my wall so they’re exactly level, even if I’m already late for a meeting.

I weigh myself every morning and sometimes again at night, and the number on the scale can make or break my whole day.

I feel compelled to wipe down surfaces before I prepare anything, wash my hands multiple times while making a meal, and if I think I touched something “greasy” or “fattening,” I’ll scrub my hands or even shower.  

These rituals are all tied to this desperate need not to gain weight. I’m not doing this with other things in my life—just with food, eating, and my body. It’s exhausting, but I feel panicky if I don’t follow these rules.
